questionText: RCTFC names five parts of a clear brief in this course. What does the first R stand for?

answerOptions.text: Role. You assign Claude a defined perspective, such as an experienced sales lead.
Research. Claude must search the internet first.
Report. Claude must format every answer as a report.
Review. You check the answer only at the end.

explanation: RCTFC stands for Role, Context, Task, Format and Constraints. The role defines a useful perspective; the other fields define the work, output and boundaries.

questionText: What is the central shift in module 1, From task to workflow?

answerOptions.text: Replace every employee with AI.
Move from manual execution to orchestration: define the work, delegate bounded steps and review the result.
Learn to write all code yourself.
Use AI only for email and nothing else.

explanation: Orchestration means picking suitable work, briefing it precisely, setting controls and checking the output. Judgement and accountability stay with you.

questionText: What stays your responsibility when Claude helps with execution?

answerOptions.text: Typing every line manually.
Only correcting spelling.
Applying judgement, deciding whether the result is suitable and accepting responsibility for its use.
Nothing. Claude takes every decision.

explanation: Delegating removes no accountability. The brief, the permissions, the factual and professional review and the decision to use the result stay with you.

questionText: Module 1 introduces three basic patterns for AI orchestration. Which set is correct?

answerOptions.text: Drafting, analysis and research.
Printing, saving and sending.
Compiling, testing and deploying.
Reading, writing and arithmetic.

explanation: The three patterns are drafting a first version, analysing supplied material and researching against defined questions. Each one still needs source and output checks that fit the task.

questionText: The AI-Native Fluency Test in module 1 uses five dimensions. Which list is correct?

answerOptions.text: Reading, writing, listening, speaking and arithmetic.
Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook and Teams.
Marketing, sales, finance, HR and IT.
Drafting, Delegation, Automation, Knowledge and Governance.

explanation: The self-assessment covers Drafting, Delegation, Automation, Knowledge and Governance across ten scenarios. It is a diagnostic exercise, not a graded qualification.

questionText: How does module 2 place Claude within a work process?

answerOptions.text: As a search engine only.
As a replacement for the whole team.
As a configurable system with defined context, bounded tasks, permissions and review.
As a chatbot used only for small talk.

explanation: Projects, Skills, plugins and MCP set context and access. People limit the permissions, check the output and stay responsible for the decision.

questionText: What is a Claude Project with standing instructions used for?

answerOptions.text: It groups relevant context, instructions and work products into a reusable workspace for a defined area of work.
It is a static file backup without working context.
It automatically deletes every conversation after 24 hours.
It is only a file backup and has no AI function.

explanation: A Project keeps instructions and reference material together, so the same context does not get typed in again for every task. Exact features and retention depend on the product version and account settings.

questionText: Connectors can link Claude to services such as Gmail, Calendar and Drive. How is access commonly authorised?

answerOptions.text: By giving Claude the email password in plain text.
Through a physical USB drive.
Connectors require no authorisation.
Through OAuth, which grants defined access without sharing the account password.

explanation: OAuth grants scoped access without handing the connected application the account password. Keep the grant to the scopes you need; the provider can normally revoke it.

questionText: What is a Skill in the Claude stack?

answerOptions.text: A badge you get for finishing a course.
A paid subscription upgrade.
An Anthropic hardware component.
A reusable instruction package for a recurring task, defined through files such as SKILL.md and supporting resources.

explanation: A Skill packages instructions and optional resources for a recurring workflow. Its exact structure depends on the product, so check the permissions and the included files before you use it.

questionText: What does MCP stand for?

answerOptions.text: Manual Copy Protocol.
Model Context Protocol, an open protocol for connecting AI applications to external tools and data sources.
Managed Cloud Platform.
Multi-Channel Posting.

explanation: MCP means Model Context Protocol. An MCP server exposes defined tools or resources to a compatible client. Connecting one expands capability and risk, so its code, transport and permissions need review.

questionText: Which project file can provide persistent instructions and conventions to Claude Code?

answerOptions.text: README.txt in the downloads folder.
A spreadsheet containing macros.
CLAUDE.md, which records maintained project context, instructions and conventions.
The Windows Registry.

explanation: CLAUDE.md is an instruction file that Claude Code can load from a project hierarchy. Keep it concise and current. It is not a place for secrets.

questionText: Which Claude Code capability is especially relevant to non-developers working with many local files?

answerOptions.text: Controlled file access and batch operations across multiple files, subject to review and permissions.
Playing music during work.
It can only be used by software developers.
Replacing the operating system.

explanation: Claude Code can run approved operations across many files instead of returning chat text only. Check the target paths, the proposed changes and the diff before you accept them.

questionText: Why does module 3 introduce an external knowledge base?

answerOptions.text: Because you should stop using your own judgement.
Because Obsidian deletes your memory.
Because AI cannot work without one.
Because work knowledge is often dispersed across messages, notes and folders and becomes more usable in a maintained, searchable system.

explanation: An external knowledge base has clear sources, links and maintenance rules. Obsidian and retrieval tools can help search it, but they do not replace source verification or ownership.

questionText: What does the PARA model used in module 3 stand for?

answerOptions.text: Plan, Act, Review, Adjust.
People, Assets, Risks, Audits.
Print, Archive, Read, Approve.
Projects, Areas, Resources and Archives, a four-part structure for organising knowledge.

explanation: PARA means Projects, Areas, Resources and Archives. Maps of Content can add navigation across those folders without requiring a complex note-taking system.

questionText: How can Smart Connections and Copilot make vault content searchable by meaning?

answerOptions.text: Through embeddings, which represent text numerically so semantically related passages can be retrieved.
Only through exact word-for-word matching like Find.
They cannot; the vault remains only a file collection.
By printing and scanning the notes.

explanation: Embeddings support semantic retrieval, which can find passages with related meaning rather than only identical words. Retrieval quality and data handling depend on the model, index and configuration.

questionText: What is the Obsidian Web Clipper used for?

answerOptions.text: Editing video.
Deleting images from the vault.
Clearing browser history.
Saving web content into the vault, optionally processing it with a template or AI-assisted interpreter.

explanation: The Web Clipper moves selected web content into the vault. A template or interpreter can structure it. The saved note keeps its source and capture date.

questionText: Why does module 4 examine self-hosting n8n?

answerOptions.text: Because self-hosting is always free.
Because self-hosting can give an organisation more control over infrastructure and data flows, while GDPR compliance still depends on contracts, configuration, access and operations.
Because n8n does not work in the cloud.
Because it never requires containers or system administration.

explanation: Self-hosting can keep selected processing within organisation-controlled infrastructure. It is not a compliance shortcut: security updates, access control, backups, logging, legal basis and processor arrangements still need assessment. This course does not provide legal advice.

questionText: In the module 4 sandbox build from email triage to a review list, what sends an incoming message down the right branch?

answerOptions.text: The printer driver.
A random selection.
A Switch node that routes the message according to the classification result.
Every message must be assigned manually before the workflow starts.

explanation: The exercise uses an example email trigger, a model call for classification and a Switch node for routing. A production version also needs confidence handling, review queues, failure paths and tests.

questionText: When does module 4 present local AI with LM Studio as an option instead of a hosted model API?

answerOptions.text: Always, because local models are necessarily better than Claude.
Never; local models are prohibited in the course.
Only for playing video.
When a reviewed architecture calls for documents to remain on controlled local infrastructure, using a suitable local model and security controls.

explanation: LM Studio can run supported models on local hardware and cut transfers to a hosted API. The choice still needs an assessment of access, model files, logs, device security, output quality and company policy.

questionText: The module 4 EU AI Act section distinguishes providers and deployers. What is a deployer?

answerOptions.text: A person who connects server hardware in a data centre.
A person or organisation that uses an AI system under its authority, except for personal non-professional activity.
Any end user, with no duties under any circumstances.
An authority that prohibits AI.

explanation: The EU AI Act defines separate roles, including provider and deployer. Applicable obligations depend on the system, risk classification, role and use. The organisation using a system under its authority is generally the deployer.

questionText: What does FRIA stand for in the EU AI Act section?

answerOptions.text: Free Risk Insurance Agreement.
Federal Reporting Information Act.
Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment, required for specified deployers and qualifying high-risk uses.
Final Review Internal Audit.

explanation: FRIA means Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment. Article 27 of the EU AI Act applies this duty to specified deployers and uses of certain high-risk systems; it is not a blanket requirement for every AI system.

questionText: What scope does the module 4 capstone brief set?

answerOptions.text: Plan, document and test one bounded workflow as a pilot with approved data; production use follows only after the required controls and approvals.
Write a 100-page theoretical paper.
Create a company ready for a stock-market listing.
Submit nothing because the capstone has no criteria.

explanation: The capstone is one small, reviewable workflow. Time budget and scope follow from availability and risk. The rubric checks documentation, measurement, failure handling and controls, not a guaranteed deployment date.

questionText: How is a capstone assessed in the workflow course?

answerOptions.text: An external jury assigns a German school grade from 1 to 6.
Through a public vote on social media.
There is no assessment scheme.
Against seven binary rubric criteria as a self-assessment, without external assessment; any publication is a separate approval decision.

explanation: The seven criteria are recorded as met or not met. No independent examiner validates the work. If an example collection is offered, publication requires explicit opt-in plus data-protection, confidentiality and security review.

questionText: What is the status of the capstone certificate of participation in the AI-Native Workflow Course?

answerOptions.text: It is an officially recognised qualification issued by an external body.
It is emailed automatically after every completed lesson.
It is a certificate of participation generated locally in the browser from your own progress and assessment, not an externally examined credential.
It is a paid add-on that must be purchased separately.

explanation: The document is created locally in your browser and confirms participation and completion. No authority and no independent examiner issues it. Its assessment state comes from your own capstone rubric or the workshop quiz.
